open_points.subject: canonical_values.content_identity ordering
open_points.text: “order-free lists sorted before hashing — ports by (`direction`, `name`), nodes by `node_id`, edges in the edge order of A05, constants by (`to_node`, `to_port`)”
open_points.question: How are edges or constants ordered when the stated sorting keys tie, as is possible for multiple guarded edges with the same endpoints or multiple constants targeting the same port, so that identity is independent of submission order?
options: Use the canonical JSON bytes of the whole item as a final tie-breaker
Preserve submission order among tied items
Refuse tied items before computing the identity
open_points.default_guess: Use the canonical JSON bytes of the whole item as a final tie-breaker.

open_points.subject: functions.add_trial_case input and expected-output maps
open_points.text: “input values by port, optional expected outputs” and “Fit in port name order — presence, carriage, schema, size”
open_points.question: Must authored trial cases contain exactly the contract's input ports and, when expected outputs are present, exactly its output ports, or are undeclared keys ignored or retained?
options: Require exactly all declared ports and no undeclared keys
Require declared ports but ignore undeclared keys
Require declared ports and retain undeclared keys in the case identity
open_points.default_guess: Require exactly all declared ports and no undeclared keys.

open_points.subject: bindings.check_installed_instances manifest validation
open_points.text: “an unreadable record, or one failing a check of the record itself (A08 rule 5), fails at its service”
open_points.question: Which A08 rule 5 checks are checks of the record itself at startup when no operation name or proposed ports are available, and must every capability entry be validated or only the record envelope and selected instance?
options: Validate only the service field, capabilities container and duplicate capability names
Validate every capability entry independently
Validate only the selected instance and ignore capabilities until proposal or send
open_points.default_guess: Validate the record envelope, duplicate capability names and selected instance, leaving operation-specific checks to proposal and send.

open_points.subject: manifest_source revision reads
open_points.question: How does `bindings` read a file at `manifest_revision`: from a Git object, from a checked-out directory that must match the revision, or through another revision-addressed manifest provider, and what failure is returned when the revision cannot be resolved?
options: Read the file directly from the named Git revision
Require `manifest_location` to be a checkout already fixed at that revision
Use a revision-addressed manifest provider defined by the installation format
open_points.default_guess: Read the file directly from the named Git revision without consulting the working tree.

open_points.subject: service_invoker base URL construction
open_points.text: “The URL is the `api_base_url` without a trailing `/` followed by the declared path”
open_points.question: Are query strings, fragments, user information, or paths allowed in `api_base_url`, and does removing “a trailing `/`” remove one slash or all trailing slashes?
options: Require an origin URL only, with no path beyond `/`, query, fragment or user information
Allow a base path but forbid query, fragment and user information, removing exactly one joining slash
Allow every absolute HTTP(S) URL and define component-aware URL joining
open_points.default_guess: Allow an optional base path, forbid query, fragment and user information, and join components with exactly one slash.

open_points.subject: plain HTTP loopback exception
open_points.text: “one whose `api_base_url` host is a loopback address”
open_points.question: What hosts count as loopback: only parsed loopback IP literals, hostnames such as `localhost`, or any hostname whose DNS result is loopback, and how are mixed DNS results handled?
options: Only IPv4 or IPv6 loopback IP literals
Loopback IP literals and the hostname `localhost`
Any hostname resolving exclusively to loopback addresses
open_points.default_guess: Only parsed IPv4 or IPv6 loopback IP literals.

open_points.subject: Port.media_type validation
open_points.text: “a `file` port declares exactly one media type”
open_points.question: What syntax and normalization rules make a media type valid, including parameters, whitespace, case, control characters and comparison, before it is emitted in HTTP headers or compared with a response Content-Type?
options: Require a parameter-free RFC media type and compare normalized type/subtype case-insensitively
Accept any bounded string and compare it exactly on flow edges
Allow parameters and define canonical parsing and comparison
open_points.default_guess: Require a parameter-free syntactically valid media type, store a canonical lowercase type/subtype, and reject controls or whitespace outside the grammar.

open_points.subject: multipart port names and filenames
open_points.text: “`Content-Disposition: form-data; name="<port>"`, with `filename="<port>"` added for a file part”
open_points.question: How are arbitrary port names encoded or escaped in multipart header parameters, and which names are refused because they cannot safely be represented?
options: Restrict multipart port names to a closed ASCII token syntax
Use the quoted-string escaping rules and reject control characters
Use RFC 5987 extended parameters for non-ASCII names
open_points.default_guess: Use quoted-string escaping, reject control characters, and encode the header as UTF-8 under one explicitly selected multipart convention.

open_points.subject: sandbox.probe_sandbox
open_points.text: “`bubblewrap` is present and one probe execution succeeds”
open_points.question: What exact code, inputs, ports, resource bounds and success conditions constitute the startup probe?
options: Run a fixed no-input function returning one fixed JSON value
Run several probes covering isolation, traps and resource enforcement
Check only that a minimal bubblewrap process starts and exits zero
open_points.default_guess: Run a release-fixed no-input function returning a fixed JSON value under release-fixed minimal bounds and require the exact expected output.

open_points.subject: surface.serve_kernel MCP entrance
open_points.text: “Start the kernel in its fixed order and serve the one MCP entrance” and “an `mcp_listen_address` that cannot be parsed or bound stops the start”
open_points.question: Which MCP transport, protocol version, endpoint path, framing and listen-address grammar does the surface implement?
options: MCP Streamable HTTP on a fixed path
MCP SSE on fixed paths
A release-defined transport selected by the installation
open_points.default_guess: Use MCP Streamable HTTP on one release-fixed endpoint, with the listen address containing only host and port.

open_points.subject: runs.continue_after_approval and runs.continue_after_resolution dependencies
open_points.text: State 3 says “A module reads what a module it may know owns through that module's capability, and never decides from another module's raw records,” but State 5 says “the approval read through `store.read_records` to find its run” and likewise reads the attempt directly.
open_points.question: How may `runs` obtain the run identity belonging to an EffectApproval or EffectAttempt without violating the State 3 ownership rule?
options: Add `effects` read capabilities that return the owning run
Require the surface request to name both the decision record and its run, with `effects` checking the relation
Declare a specific exception allowing `runs` to read approval and attempt records directly
open_points.default_guess: Add `effects` capabilities that resolve an approval or attempt to its owning run.

open_points.subject: functions.add_captured_trial_case SpooledFile lookup
open_points.text: State 3 says `runs` passes “spooled files as their SpooledFiles,” while State 5 says `functions` checks each file “read from its SpooledFile through `store.read_records`.”
open_points.question: Does `functions` trust the complete SpooledFile facts passed by `runs`, or independently read records owned and produced by `runs` or `effects` through `store`?
options: Trust the complete SpooledFile models passed by `runs` and read only their bytes
Add a `runs` capability for resolving checked spooled-file records
Permit `functions` to read SpooledFile records directly from `store`
open_points.default_guess: Trust the complete SpooledFile models passed by `runs`, then use `store.read_value_bytes` only after all checks pass.

open_points.subject: EffectApproval refusal trace inputs
open_points.text: “`effects.decide_effect_approval`” takes “An approval identity, approve or refuse, the actor” but on refusal writes “the element's NodeExecution `refused_by_owner`.”
open_points.question: Where does `decide_effect_approval` obtain the exact StoredValue and SpooledFile references required for that NodeExecution's `inputs`, since M24 fixes only input digests and a preview and the operation receives no element inputs?
options: Store the exact input references in EffectApproval
Have `runs` pass the element's input references when deciding
Let `effects` reconstruct the references from run records
open_points.default_guess: Store the exact input references in EffectApproval and use them when writing the refusal record.

open_points.subject: get_repair_view continuation token
open_points.text: “a continuation token that also carries the implementation set of its first page” together with “every other string anywhere in the request, at most `bounded_text_bytes_max`”
open_points.question: What happens when a slot has enough implementations that the frozen implementation set cannot fit in a continuation token that can later pass the request string bound?
options: Store paging snapshots server-side and issue a bounded random token
Give the token a separate larger bound
Refuse or truncate the repair page when the implementation set is too large
open_points.default_guess: Store a durable bounded paging snapshot and return a bounded opaque token naming it.
